transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I came in because I just seem to worry about everything lately. I'm a real estate agent, and I'm constantly stressing about my clients, the market, money... but it's also my family, and even little things, like whether moving into my new condo was the right decision. It just feels like my worrying is completely out of proportion to what's actually happening.
Have you experienced any panic attacks recently?
No, I haven't. I just feel constantly wound up, but I haven't had anything like a full-blown panic attack.
Have you been avoiding any situations or activities because of your worrying?

No, I wouldn't say I'm avoiding anything. I still go to work, show houses, and see my family. I haven't stopped my normal routine or anything like that. I just... well, I just worry the whole time I'm doing those things. But I still do them.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches or muscle tension?

Yes, I have noticed some muscle tension. By the end of the day, my neck and shoulders feel really tight, kind of like I’ve been bracing myself. And sometimes I'll actually catch myself clenching my jaw, especially when I’m driving between listings or just sitting at my desk.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?
No, not really. I don't feel sad. It's... well, it's really just the worrying. My mood is fine for the most part, I just feel stressed out and on edge, not down.
Has your worrying affected your performance at work or your relationships with family and friends?

Well, with my family and friends, things are mostly the same. But at work... yes, it has. Even straightforward things, like listing negotiations and contract reviews, are just taking me much longer than they used to. I've actually had to delay returning calls lately because... well, I just don't feel confident that I've checked everything carefully enough before I talk to them.
Is your worrying mostly about one or two specific things, or is it about a wide range of topics?

It's definitely a wide range. That's actually why I came in, because I just seem to worry about everything now. It's my clients, the market, my family, money... I even worry about whether moving to the condo was the right decision. It's just a lot of different topics, and honestly, it feels out of proportion to what is actually happening.
How long have you been experiencing this excessive worrying?
It's been going on for about a year and two months now. It really started right after I sold my longtime house and moved into the condo.
Do you often feel restless or have trouble sitting still when you're worrying?
No, not really. I don't feel restless or feel like I need to move around. I can sit still just fine, I just... I just have all these thoughts running through my head.
Has your excessive worrying about these various topics persisted for most days over the past year, or have there been periods where it significantly decreased?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't kept track of it day by day. It feels like it's just always kind of there in the background since I moved, but... I don't know if there were specific periods where it significantly decreased. I just haven't really noticed or measured it like that.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking or rechecking things, like locks or your work, as part of your worrying?

No, I don't really do that. I mean, I'll double-check my work documents just to be thorough—you have to be careful with real estate contracts—but I don't repeatedly check things like locks or... or go back over things multiple times because of the worry. It's really just the thoughts themselves, not me doing things like that.
Do you have any recurring, intrusive thoughts that you try to ignore or suppress?

No, I wouldn't say so. It's not like I have specific, unwanted thoughts that just pop into my head that I have to fight off or ignore. It's really just... a steady stream of regular worries, you know? Just thinking a bit too much about everyday things, like my clients or the move, but it's nothing I'm actively trying to suppress.
Would you say that your worrying is causing you a lot of distress?

Well, yes, it is. It's starting to really affect my work. Even just straightforward things, like listing negotiations or reviewing contracts, they're taking me so much longer than they used to. I find myself putting off returning client calls because I just don't feel confident that I've looked over everything carefully enough yet. It's frustrating.
Has your excessive worrying affected your relationships with friends or made social interactions more difficult for you?

No, I haven't really noticed that. My friendships are fine. I mean, I still see people and socialize like I normally would. It hasn't really gotten in the way of my personal relationships or anything... it's mostly just my work and my own peace of mind that are taking the hit. Socially, I think I'm doing okay.
Do you often feel like you're on edge, even when there's no immediate reason for it?

No, not really. I don't feel keyed up or on edge like that. It's really just the worrying itself that's the problem, not a physical feeling of being on edge or restless. I just can't seem to turn my brain off when it comes to the things I'm stressed about.
Have you ever had a panic attack in your life, even if it was not recently?
No, I've never had a panic attack. I know what those are, but I've never experienced one myself. It's really just this constant worrying about work that's been bothering me.
Do you feel like your worrying is accompanied by a sense of restlessness or feeling on edge?

No, like I mentioned a minute ago, I don't really get that feeling. I'm not restless or, you know, physically on edge. It really is just the thoughts in my head that won't stop, but my body feels fine. I don't have that restless energy.
Has your worrying significantly impacted your ability to function effectively in your daily life or at work?

Yes, it has, especially at work. I've been a real estate broker for a long time, but lately... well, even straightforward listing negotiations and contract reviews are taking me much longer than they used to. I've even had to delay returning phone calls because I just don't feel confident that I've checked everything carefully enough. So it is definitely slowing me down and making things harder than they need to be.
